quarterly_data.signal: New calendar-2030 targets presented by the CFO at the SEMICON West investor breakfast (Applied is not giving a WFE forecast, saying it changes at a rapid rate): outgrow WFE and gain more than 2 percentage points of WFE share across the horizon (equipment business to be modeled as growing faster than the industry); Applied Global Services at a mid-teens CAGR, modeled as greater than $12 billion by 2030; Other revenue (display incl. MaxOLED, plus the SENZ waveguide photonics business) more than $2 billion by 2030; 54% non-GAAP gross margin and 40% non-GAAP operating margin; 15% estimated tax rate for 2030; committed to 80%-100% return distributions of free cash flow over time while reinvesting more than 50% of cash generated in the business.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 2 percentage points of WFE share; Applied Global Services greater than $12 billion by 2030; Other more than $2 billion by 2030; 54% non-GAAP gross margin; 40% non-GAAP operating margin; 15% estimated tax rate for 2030; 80%-100% of free cash flow returned

quarterly_data.signal: CFO on the path to the 2030 margin targets: 54% gross margin means approximately 100 basis points each year, though not a smooth ride - Applied must invest in a new factory and logistics, and there are cost headwinds (fuel costs, rare earths); Applied is raising pricing as part of its value-pricing process to address those costs. The 40% operating margin comes from four additional points on the gross margin plus 200-300 basis points in operating leverage, with AI automation letting corporate functions and SG&A scale at high productivity. Free cash flow has averaged more than 21%; no target, but the CFO expects it 'a little bit higher'. Track record cited: over 10 years revenue grew at a 12.2% revenue CAGR to $34.3 billion, non-GAAP gross margin rose 680 basis points to 50%, non-GAAP operating margin rose over 1,100 basis points, EPS CAGR 22%; R&D grew from over $1 billion to over $4 billion ($4.2 billion, 72% of spending) while operating spending fell from 22% of revenue to 17% today. Internal AI use: AI-assisted hardware development pilots achieved more than 4X and are being implemented on 20 products; 100% of software developers use AI with a 44% average productivity gain.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 100 basis points each year; four additional points on the gross margin; 200-300 basis points in operating leverage; more than 21% free cash flow average; 12.2% revenue CAGR to $34.3 billion; 680 basis points to 50%; over 1,100 basis points; R&D $4.2 billion, 72% of spending; operating spending 22% to 17% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and constraints: CEO Gary Dickerson said Applied is investing to double its lab capacity and double its manufacturing capacity 'from even today, so higher than the last time I said that'; the CFO said capacity from a manufacturing and lab perspective grows more than 2X across the horizon, with CapEx approximately 8% of revenue this year and declining as a percentage of revenue. Investments named: the EPIC Center (largest investment), Arizona, Massachusetts and Texas (Applied's largest manufacturing site), new manufacturing capacity and labs in Italy and Israel, R&D and supply-chain investments in India, a second Singapore manufacturing facility just opened, customer-facing investments in South Korea and Taiwan. CFO: fab utilization is 100% in leading-edge logic, 100% in DRAM and almost 100% in NAND, ICAPS healthy after digestion; clean room is the primary constraint, with data center energy availability and supply chain also pacing growth (CEO adds fab space, supply chain components, energy and financing); Applied raised its forecast to its supply chain every single quarter this year and sees pinch points to manage but no roadblocks over the medium term.
quarterly_data.figure: double lab and manufacturing capacity (more than 2X); CapEx approximately 8% of revenue this year; fab utilization leading-edge logic 100%, DRAM 100%, NAND almost 100%

quarterly_data.signal: Demand framework: CEO said Applied saw significant growth in agentic AI compute demand in calendar 2026 and has increased its wafer fab equipment forecast going forward because of it (no WFE number given); an agentic AI factory pod consumes about 2-4 times more wafers than a generative AI pod (Rubin and Rubin Ultra configurations), and 85% of the content of the agentic AI factory by wafer starts is leading-edge foundry logic, DRAM and advanced packaging; server CPU, GPU, networking and ASIC chips are moving to the leading edge faster. Semiconductor Products Group President Prabu Raja: Applied's SAM is around 55% of the WFE market, and around 75% of all WFE growth through 2030 is expected in leading-edge foundry logic, DRAM and advanced packaging, where Applied is number one; Applied expects to gain over 2 percentage market points of WFE share by 2030, and raised several SAM numbers because more process steps (treatments, anneals, thermal interface materials) are being ordered.
quarterly_data.figure: agentic AI pod about 2-4 times more wafers than a generative AI pod; 85% of agentic AI factory content; Applied SAM around 55% of WFE; around 75% of WFE growth through 2030 in three segments; over 2 percentage points of WFE share by 2030

quarterly_data.signal: China and share math: CEO said the 2030 share target still models growth in China, including restricted accounts where Applied cannot serve leading edge, DRAM or NAND, and assumes no change in trade rules; excluding those, the share gain would be greater. CFO: Applied had access to 100% of China's WFE market in the early 2020s, which dropped to 90%, and in 2025 went from 90 to closer to 70; adjusting for trade restrictions Applied's share is up, and in China at 28 nanometers Applied is doing very well.
quarterly_data.figure: China WFE access 100% (early 2020s), then 90%, closer to 70 in 2025

quarterly_data.signal: Leading-edge logic (Prabu Raja): Applied's leading-edge SAM grows from around $12 billion at 3 nanometers to $15 billion at 1.4 nanometers, with Applied's share rising by 3 points over the transition (CEO: WFE per wafer start rises node over node from 5 nanometer to 1.4 nanometer, with Applied's addressable market growing to more than 50% through that period). Co-optimized transistor-contact solutions (etch, CVD and epi) deliver a 5% performance gain against customers' 15% node-over-node target and are expected to deliver over $2 billion cumulative revenue for Applied until 2030; copper wiring products will deliver $3 billion revenue in 2026; integrated solution portfolio revenue 'grew 20% to 30% of our system revenue today'; 13 new products launched in the last 12 months for transistor, wiring and advanced packaging. Over 60% of the materials on a chip are created by Applied equipment. From a mobile chip to an agentic AI chip, logic silicon area grows 70 times, logic transistors 20x and wiring layers triple. CEO: Applied is about 2.5 times larger than its nearest competitor in deposition, greater than 2 times in materials modification and about 2 times in E-beam, and a leader in conductor etch.
quarterly_data.figure: leading-edge SAM $12 billion at 3 nanometers to $15 billion at 1.4 nanometers, share up 3 points; over $2 billion cumulative revenue until 2030; copper wiring $3 billion revenue in 2026; integrated solution portfolio 'grew 20% to 30% of our system revenue'; 13 new products in 12 months

quarterly_data.signal: Metrology and inspection (Keith Wells, head of the Imaging and Process Control Group): Applied expects '$3 billion in systems and service revenue in 2026' for M&I, with very high growth going forward; optical inspection and E-beam revenue each grow 50% from 2025 to 2026. Optical inspection is a $9 billion market of which Applied serves only about $2 billion today; new optical products over the next few years target the $7 billion of additional TAM, where customers want alternatives to incumbents. In E-beam, cold field emission technology gave Applied 2X revenue over its nearest competitor; many new E-beam tools are planned over the next few years. A new on-device, in-line X-ray materials metrology capability (built on CFE) is now used at customers; Applied puts that new market at several hundred million dollars, not yet in its P&L.
quarterly_data.figure: M&I $3 billion systems and service revenue in 2026; optical and E-beam each +50% from 2025 to 2026; optical inspection market $9 billion, Applied serves about $2 billion; $7 billion additional TAM; E-beam 2X revenue over nearest competitor; new X-ray metrology market several hundred million dollars

quarterly_data.signal: Applied Global Services (Tim Deane, head of AGS): AIX-connected chambers expected to grow from 37,000 today to over 90,000 by calendar year 2030, with about 80% remotely connected; more than 18 quarters of data show 30% faster service resolutions on AIX-connected tools; long-term contracts currently greater than 2.5 years with a more than 90% renewal rate (AIX services renew at higher rates than service overall); subscription rates rising from the low 40% to nearly 70% in the 2030 plan; 20% revenue per tool growth between 2025 and 2030; AIX CrossMatch now ramps tool matching 50% faster, and a Gen 2 model predicts electrostatic-chuck failures 30 days in advance with more than 90% accuracy. CFO: the installed base is in the high 50,000s tools, growing 5%-10% per year, with the rest of the mid-teens growth from new service products.
quarterly_data.figure: connected chambers 37,000 to over 90,000 by calendar year 2030; about 80% remote; contracts greater than 2.5 years; more than 90% renewal rate; subscription from low 40% to nearly 70%; 20% revenue per tool growth 2025-2030; installed base high 50,000s tools growing 5%-10% per year

quarterly_data.signal: Adjacent businesses (CEO): display and SENZ together run at around $400 million per quarter and should not be modeled beyond that near term; display earns a little over 20% operating profit; MaxOLED, which eliminates the fine metal mask so OLED can move to IT, TV and automotive sizes, is being implemented with leading display companies as yields are brought to the high-volume tipping point; display deposition and E-beam leadership is being brought into semiconductor panel packaging. SENZ waveguides for AI glasses: around 90% of the flow is Applied custom innovation, and the strategy is to sell waveguides and eyepieces. CFO: the two businesses are expected to be more than $2 billion by 2030.
quarterly_data.figure: around $400 million per quarter run rate; display a little over 20% operating profit; around 90% of waveguide flow Applied custom; more than $2 billion by 2030

quarterly_data.signal: ICAPS (Prabu Raja): power and photonics for the data center build-out are growing very rapidly and Applied expects over $1 billion revenue from them this year; the ICAPS market is growing this year, helped by nodes transitioning to 28-nanometer transistors where Applied is well positioned with High-k/metal gate, and physical AI is expected to be a big future ICAPS growth driver. CEO: photonics and power is a very fast-growing business, with hybrid bonding an important innovation there.
quarterly_data.figure: power and photonics over $1 billion revenue this year

quarterly_data.signal: DRAM roadmap (Prabu Raja): Applied said in the past 6F² would be around $6 billion, and 'from 6F² to 4F², I think it is increasing over 40%', with 3D DRAM higher still, and Applied expects to increase its SAM share by 5 points; the number of wiring layers more than doubles from conventional DRAM to HBM DRAM. CEO: Applied's served market in advanced DRAM grows to more than 60% and Applied gained around 10 points of overall DRAM share over a number of years; he believes the three companies leading in DRAM today will continue to lead. CFO on HBM de-specing: system architects are tuning memory per workload, and Applied expects DRAM to remain constrained for a period of time; CEO adds that training still wants the tallest stacks and the new workloads are additive, a repartitioning rather than cannibalization.
quarterly_data.figure: 6F² SAM around $6 billion, up over 40% to 4F²; SAM share up 5 points; served market more than 60%; around 10 points of DRAM share gained

quarterly_data.signal: HBM packaging (Prabu Raja): Applied enables three-quarters of the HBM packaging process steps, from TSV formation to micro bumps on both wafer sides, and is number one in HBM packaging with more than 60% SAM share; 'HBM continues to grow, and we expect over $1 billion this year alone.' Hybrid bonding is the next big HBM inflection and will double Applied's SAM compared with micro bumps and TSV.
quarterly_data.figure: three-quarters of HBM packaging steps; more than 60% SAM share; over $1 billion this year; hybrid bonding to double SAM

contracts.signal: AGS head Tim Deane: 'Manish and Micron have been a great partner as we fanned AIX out into their factories' - Applied's AIX AI-enabled service platform deployed across Micron's fabs.

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced packaging (Prabu Raja): Applied's advanced packaging business is now expected to grow to more than $5 billion within a few years, and Applied expects to outgrow the market over the next 5 years as its on-chip wiring technologies move to chip-to-chip wiring (micro bumps, bumps, TSVs). In hybrid bonding Applied's portfolio addresses 80% of the steps across pre-bonding, bonding and post-bonding, partnering with Besi for the die-to-wafer bonding step (Kinex integrated tool); hybrid bonding is already adopted in HBM, 3D IC logic and co-packaged optics. For the silicon-interposer-to-panel transition Applied has built organic and inorganic panel portfolios through the Tango, panel PVD, NEXX (panel copper plating) acquisitions and Sigray for X-ray.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced packaging more than $5 billion within a few years; hybrid bonding portfolio addresses 80% of the steps

quarterly_data.signal: Packaging inspection (Keith Wells): the optical inspection market for advanced packaging went from a few hundred million a couple of years ago to well over $1 billion as customers inspect every die before placement; Applied started a completely new, cost-effective optical inspection platform for it and says it will be differentiated with the highest sensitivity at the highest throughput, after about a year and a half studying the market. Applied's front-end E-beam products adapted for back-end packaging are already generating revenue across multiple products, and customers now accept higher ASPs to meet packaging yield demands.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced packaging optical inspection market from a few hundred million to well over $1 billion
